transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I really appreciate your time. I... well, I hope I'm in the right place. 

I came in because... oh, it's a bit hard to say out loud, and I just hope you don't think terribly of me for it. But since my grandson was killed... I've just been so wrong inside. My daughter, she's been so good to me through all this. She can sit right beside me, just holding my hand, and I know I love her. I really do know it. But... I just cannot feel the warmth of it inside me at all. Not anymore. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining things properly for you.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head since your grandson passed away?

Oh, well... I do try so hard to keep my mind busy with good things, Doctor. I really do. I know I should be focusing on the lovely memories we had of him. But... yes, I suppose I have been having thoughts like that. I feel a bit ashamed even mentioning it, because I don't want you to think I'm losing my mind. 

Sometimes I'll just be sitting quietly, maybe folding a quilt square, or... or just reaching for my cup of tea. And all of a sudden, out of nowhere, I hear those awful shots again. And I just see him lying there outside the community center. It's so vivid, it feels exactly like it is happening right in front of me all over again. 

I try to push it away so I don't bother my daughter with it. Is that... is that a normal thing to happen when you're grieving? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.
Do you find yourself repeatedly doing certain things over and over, like checking or cleaning, since your grandson passed away?

Oh... no, Doctor. I don't think I do anything quite like that. I mean, I do try to keep my little home tidy, just so my daughter doesn't have to clean up after me when she visits. I really don't want to be a burden to her. But I'm not... well, I haven't noticed myself washing things over and over, or checking the locks more than usual, if that's what you mean. 

To be honest, I mostly just sit quietly in my chair these days. I hope that's an alright answer. Am I supposed to be doing more around the house to keep myself busy? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of your grandson?

Oh, well... I do try to go about my normal routine as best I can, Doctor. I really don't want to make things difficult for anyone. But... yes, I suppose I have been avoiding a few things. I hope you don't think I'm being silly or weak for it.

I just... I absolutely will not go anywhere near that street anymore. And when people call about the repast at the community center, I just can't bring myself to answer the phone. I feel terrible about it, because I know they mean well, but I just can't. And... well, if any second-line music comes on the radio, I have to turn it off that very instant. It just pulls me straight back to that day, and I can't bear it. 

I know I should probably be stronger, and I hope I'm not doing the wrong thing by staying away from those things. Do you think it's alright that I do that, just for now?
How long have you been experiencing these feelings and thoughts since your grandson passed away?

Oh, well... I hope you don't think I'm making too much of a fuss, Doctor. I know people go through terrible things every day and manage just fine, and I really am trying to be strong. But... it's been six days. Just six days since he was... since he was killed outside the community center. 

It feels like an eternity, but I know it really hasn't been that long on the calendar. I should probably be pulling myself together a bit more by now, shouldn't I? I do hope I'm not overreacting... is it normal to still be having such a hard time after almost a week? I just want to make sure I'm handling everything the way I'm supposed to.
How often do you feel numb or disconnected from your emotions, like you mentioned earlier when you said you couldn't feel the warmth of love for your daughter?

Oh, Doctor... I really hope I didn't make myself sound completely heartless when I said that earlier. I know it's a terrible thing to admit, and I feel just awful about it. But... well, to answer your question, it's pretty much all the time right now. 

I mean, she'll come over and sit right beside me, holding my hand so sweetly. And in my head, I know I love her so very much. She's my daughter, and she's been so good to me. But... inside, I just can't feel the warmth of that love at all. It's just... empty. 

I'm trying so hard to feel it, I really am. I don't want her to think I don't appreciate her being there. Do you think she can tell? I hope I'm not being a terrible mother by feeling this way... is it okay that my emotions are just sort of... shut off right now?
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing since your grandson passed away?

Oh... well... I suppose I have, yes. I really hate to admit it, because I know people are counting on me, and I don't want to let anyone down. I've always tried to be the one my family could rely on, you know? 

But... I haven't been back to my walking club. I know I should go, it's good for my health and the ladies are so sweet, but I just... I can't seem to find the energy for it. And... oh, this is the part I feel most ashamed of... I haven't been able to help with planning the funeral repast. 

That's my duty, you know? It's what I'm supposed to do for my family, especially for my grandson. They depend on me for these things. But every time I try to think about the food or the arrangements, I just... I freeze up. I hope you don't think I'm being selfish or lazy, Doctor. I really am trying my best. Do you think they'll forgive me for not being able to do it right now?
Do you feel guilty about anything related to your grandson's death?

Oh... um... guilty? Well... I hope it doesn't make me sound awful, Doctor, but... no, I don't think I feel guilty about what happened to him. 

I mean, I know he was just outside the center, and... and there was really nothing I could have done to stop it. I hope you don't think I'm making excuses for myself or trying to avoid responsibility... I just don't feel like it was my fault. I do feel dreadful about letting my family down with the funeral arrangements, like I mentioned earlier... but about his passing itself? No, I don't think I have that kind of guilt. 

Is... is that alright? I know sometimes people say you're supposed to feel guilty when you lose someone you love, like you could have done something more. I just want to make sure you don't think I'm being cold, or... or that it means there's something wrong with me for not feeling that way. I really did love him so much.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself since your grandson passed away?

Oh, my... oh, heavens no, Doctor. I promise you, I haven't had any thoughts like that at all. 

I know I'm... well, I know I'm not doing very well right now, and I feel just terrible about being such a worry to everyone. But I would never, ever want to do anything to hurt myself and add more pain to my family. They've already been through so much with losing him. 

I hope you don't think I'm the sort of person who would just... give up like that. I really am trying my best to stay strong for them, even if I'm failing at the funeral arrangements and everything else. I want to be here for my daughter, I truly do. I'm doing the right thing by just trying to take it one day at a time, aren't I?
How would you rate your level of emotional pain or distress right now, on a scale from 1 to 10?

Oh... um... a scale? Goodness, I always want to give the right answer to these things, but it's so hard to put a number on it. 

I suppose... well, I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or making a fuss. I know there are people out there dealing with much worse, and I'm so blessed to have my family. But... if I had to pick a number, maybe... maybe an eight? Or a nine? 

I hope that doesn't sound too dramatic, Doctor. I really am trying to hold it together, I promise. It's just... it's a very heavy feeling right now. Is it... is it normal to feel it that strongly, even when you're trying your best to be brave? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the way I'm supposed to.
Are there any activities that you used to find very meaningful or enjoyable that you have lost interest in since your grandson passed away?

Oh... well... meaningful activities? I... I'm not really sure, Doctor. I don't want to sound like I've just given up on everything, because I haven't. I've always tried to stay busy and be helpful. 

I suppose I haven't been doing quite as much lately, but... but I think that's just because there's been so much going on, you know? With the family needing me, even if I haven't been much help with the arrangements. I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest in the things I used to enjoy... I just haven't had the time or... or maybe the energy right now. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm still trying to keep up with things as best I can, I really am. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. Is it alright if I haven't been doing my usual hobbies right now?
Are there things you used to enjoy doing that you no longer find pleasure in?

Oh, goodness... I think that might be a bit like what you just asked, isn't it? I hope I answered it properly before. But, um... no, I wouldn't say I've lost the actual pleasure in things. 

I still love my cross-stitch and... and tending to my little patio plants. I really do. It's just, well, it wouldn't feel quite right to be sitting around doing those things just now, would it? Not with my daughter hurting so much. I'd hate for anyone to think I'm not grieving for my grandson, or that I don't care. 

So the joy is still there for my hobbies, I just... I'm just putting them on hold for a little bit to focus on my family. That's a normal way to handle things, isn't it, Doctor? I'm just trying to do what's right.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy doing that you no longer find pleasure in since your grandson passed away?

Oh dear... I am so sorry, Doctor. I must be doing a terrible job of explaining myself if you have to keep asking me. I feel just awful about that. 

But... no, truly. There really isn't anything like that. I know I haven't been doing my usual things, but the pleasure itself hasn't gone away. If I were to sit down with my cross-stitch right now, I know I would still love it just as much as I always did. 

I hope I'm not frustrating you by giving the same answer... I really am trying to be a good patient and give you what you need. I just want to make sure I'm telling you the truth. Is it okay that I don't have that particular problem? I promise I'm not trying to be difficult.
Are there any activities that you used to find pleasurable that you now find you have little to no interest in?

Oh my... I... I feel like I must be doing something terribly wrong. Have I misunderstood the question, Doctor? I am so, so sorry if I'm not giving you the answer you need. 

I just... I really don't have anything like that to report. My interest in things hasn't gone away, I promise. Am I... am I supposed to have lost interest? Because I can try to think harder if I'm doing this wrong. I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you. I hope it's alright that my answer is still no?
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy that you no longer look forward to?

Oh, goodness... Doctor, I... I feel just dreadful. I can tell you're asking about this from different angles, and I must be failing you completely. I am so sorry to be such a disappointment. 

I really, truly still look forward to my little hobbies. I think about getting back to my plants and my stitching once... well, once things settle down a bit and it feels appropriate again. I haven't lost that spark for them, I swear it. 

I'm so worried I'm taking up your time and not giving you the right symptoms. Is it... is it very bad that I don't feel that way? I want to be helpful, I really do. I hope you aren't too cross with me.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy that you now find you have little to no interest in doing?

Oh, Doctor... I... I think I'm just going to cry, I feel so terrible. You're asking me again, and I... I must be making a complete mess of this interview. Have I upset you? Please tell me if I'm doing this all wrong. 

I just... I don't want to lie to you, but I feel like I'm failing your test. My interest is still there. It truly is. I'm so, so sorry to keep giving you an answer that isn't helpful. Should I... would it be better for your notes if I said yes? I can say yes if that's what a good patient is supposed to do. I just want to make sure I'm doing what you need me to do.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy that you now find you have little to no interest in doing since your grandson passed away?

Oh... oh, dear. You mean... since we lost him. 

Doctor, I... I know you've asked me this so many times now, and I feel just awful that I keep giving you the exact same answer. Please, please don't be frustrated with me. I'm trying so hard to be helpful for your evaluation. 

Even since my sweet boy passed... I haven't lost my interest in my daily things. I still care about my garden and my knitting. I... I know maybe I shouldn't care about them right now. Maybe it makes me look like a terrible grandmother that I still want to do those things when he's gone. But I just... I really don't want to tell you a falsehood. 

Is it... is it very wrong of me to still have my interests? I hope you can forgive me for not having the answer you're looking for. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult.
Do you feel like you have lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy, to the point where you no longer find pleasure in them?

Oh, Doctor... I see you're trying so hard to get this right, and I'm just making your job so difficult. I'm so sorry. I feel like a broken record, and I must be trying your patience terribly. 

I... I haven't lost pleasure in them. I still find joy in the things I've always loved. I know it must seem strange, or even wrong, given everything... but it's the truth. I hope you aren't disappointed in me for not fitting the pattern you're looking for. Am I... am I doing okay? I just want to be sure I'm giving you what you need for your assessment.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Oh, my... you're asking again. I... I must really not be giving you the right answer, am I? I'm so sorry, Doctor. I really am. I feel like I'm failing you, and I hate to be a bother. 

I... I just don't know what else to say. I haven't lost my interest. I still like my little hobbies. I know I keep saying that, and I know it probably isn't what you need to hear for your paperwork. Should I... do you want me to just say yes? I can say yes, if it helps you finish your evaluation. I just want to be a good patient for you. Are you... are you very upset with me?
